channel.title: TalkLive Blog
channel.description: Guides and research on talking to strangers, voice chat, language practice and online safety - from the team behind TalkLive.

item.title: Why It Is Sometimes Easier to Tell a Stranger the Truth
item.description: People confess things to strangers on trains that they never tell their friends. A sociologist noticed this in 1908. Here is what is going on, and where it stops working.

item.title: The Rise and Fall of Omegle: Fourteen Years of Talking to Strangers
item.description: An 18-year-old built Omegle in his bedroom in 2009. It closed in November 2023 with a note about cost, misuse and a heart attack in his thirties. How it got there, and what it left behind.

item.title: We Are Bad at Predicting How Talking to Strangers Will Feel
item.description: Commuters, coffee queues and first conversations: a decade of experiments shows people consistently underestimate how much they will enjoy talking to strangers. Six studies, and their limits.

item.title: Loneliness Is Not the Same as Being Alone
item.description: You can be lonely in a full house and content on your own. What loneliness really is, why it makes people pull away, and the surprising finding about which kinds of help work best.

item.title: What Actually Happens in the Two Seconds After You Press "Start"
item.description: A plain-English tour of a random voice match: the waiting queue, why filters make you wait, the handshake that connects two browsers, and the relay that carries the audio when a direct line is impossible.

item.title: Listening Is a Skill. Most of Us Were Never Taught It.
item.description: Why we interrupt, the "shift response" that quietly steals conversations, and what research says about the single habit that makes people like you more. Ten questions about listening.

item.title: "Why Does My Heart Race Every Time the Phone Rings?"
item.description: A reader cannot make or answer phone calls without dread. Our reply on why calls are genuinely harder than texting, the habit that keeps the fear alive, and a step-by-step ladder out of it.

item.title: Why You Understand More Than You Can Say
item.description: Most learners can follow far more than they can say. A linguist called this out in 1985. Field notes on why speaking is its own skill, the fear that blocks it, and a four-week routine.

item.title: A Field Guide to the Scams That Start With "Hi"
item.description: Romance-to-crypto schemes, sextortion, the "send me the code" trick and the bots that never answer a question. Seven common specimens, how to recognise each, and the one rule that defeats nearly all of them.

item.title: 30 Questions That Get Past Small Talk
item.description: In 1997 a psychologist made strangers feel close in 45 minutes with a list of questions that slowly got deeper. The idea behind it, why "what do you do?" stalls, and thirty questions in three tiers.
